findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Not done: src/forge/release-notes/v1.2.50.md lists every client-visible change merged since v1.2.49 and the release notes tests pass; nothing else changes
Case: normal use - a team upgrades, asks a code question from a different agent family, or relies on the runner to report a stopped item.
The notes contain material inaccuracies. Line 12 says code-question explorers follow `workers`, but `src/forge/roles.py:155-175` creates the native explorer separately for each chat host, so a Codex chat still uses its Codex explorer when `workers = "claude"`. Line 17 says the runner merges work, but `src/forge/repo.py:574` defaults to human merges and `src/forge/land.py:208-215` stops at a pull request. Line 18 promises desktop notices without saying Windows receives none: `src/forge/stops.py:150-152` returns without sending one. A Windows owner waiting for that notice can leave a question or merge waiting. These source details are new evidence beyond the coordinator's note that the tests passed.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test: src/forge/release-notes/v1.2.50.md lists every client-visible change merged since v1.2.49 and the release notes tests pass; nothing else changes
Case: normal use - an upgrade shows a misleading release note while the named proof passes.
The coordinator reported that `tests/test_release_notes.py` passed, but the proof does not establish the notes' completeness or accuracy. Its tag-push test accepts a synthetic v9.9.9 bullet, and its upgrade assertions at lines 138-155 check fixture bullets and older release files, not the v1.2.50 claims. The suite can therefore pass with the current incorrect explorer, merge, and Windows-notice statements, or with the new bullets omitted. That coverage gap is evidence the coordinator's pass-only note did not address.
findings.title: Test: v1.2.50 release notes list every client-visible change

why: The v1.2.50 release notes miss what merged after the first notes were written: the explorer follows the builder, typed approval in Codex chats, review severity and pending-after-merge proof, the Codex cache-safe effort change and chat shortening, the queue runner with its notices and stops, and the settings-fix guide rule.
